text: **Lush green or golden fields** can be found in this band from the south of the Yorke Peninsula to Echuca. clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Kangaroo Island Landscape

In addition, the island only has Generation 2 and Generation 4 coverage, with Generation 2 being most common.

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Darwin Landscape

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Western South Australia Landscape
text: The area around Warramboo in SA to Madura in WA has a unique landscape. Vegetation is quite **dry** and is made up of shrubs and **wide crowned eucalyptus**. In addition, the soil is sandy with a slight orange tint.
The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has a similar landscape, with the same vegetation but usually with whiter soil.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Eastern South Australia Landscape
text: The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has quite **dry vegetation** and is made up of shrubs and **wide cronwed eucalyptus**. In addition, the soil is sandy with a white tint.
Western South Australia has a similar landscape, but with orangish soil.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Northern Queensland Landscape

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Agriculture - Sugarcane

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Inland New South Wales Landscape
text: The landscape in inland NSW is mostly flat, and the soil gets redder the more inland you go. Vegetation consists of mostly dry pale-green shrubs. Further east and on the Queensland and Victorian borders, the climate gets more temperate but is still quite dry and more eucalyptus trees can be seen, with the soil transitioning into a more sandy colour as well as more hills being visible.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Tasmania Landscape
text: Tasmania has a **cool temperate** climate which is uncommon in the rest of Australia and is comparable to central-southern Chile or New Zealand. Typical landscape consists of green rolling hills that can look dry in winter coverage. Eucalyptus trees can be seen on the side of roads and on hills in the distance. Rural Tasmania is also quite hilly with dense eucalyptus forests making up the landscape.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Kangaroo Island

clues.title: Landscape: Southwest South Australia Landscape
text: The area around Warramboo in SA to Madura in WA has a unique landscape. Vegetation is quite dry and is made up of shrubs and wide crowned eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a slight orange tint. The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has a similar landscape, with the same vegetation but usually with whiter soil.
NOTE: The soil gets more red in the WA side. Redder soil can also be seen more inland on the Victorian side around Mildura.

clues.title: Landscape: South Fields

In the SA side, the landscape should be drier than the Victorian side and more wide crowned eucalyptus can be seen. On the Victorian side, the trees generally have more leaves and are taller.

clues.title: Landscape: Cocos Islands

clues.title: Landscape: Tasmania
text: Tasmania has a cool temperate climate which is uncommon in the rest of Australia and is comparable to central-southern Chile or New Zealand. Typical landscape consists of green rolling hills that can look dry in winter coverage. Eucalyptus trees can be seen on the side of roads and on hills in the distance. Rural Tasmania is also quite hilly with dense eucalyptus forests making up the landscape.
NOTE: Certain areas of Victoria can look similar so make sure to look for other clues.
